**Justin Thomas — Make Cut +107 (Pinnacle)**

Here's why: JT's model make-cut probability is 64.5%, but the book has him at 48.3%. That's a 16-point edge — the biggest gap on the board this week.

The underlying case is solid. He's got OTT +0.66/round (#23 in field), which is above average. More importantly, his form is rising — he's made 5 straight cuts and picked up +0.23 strokes over his last five starts. At the U.S. Open, where tee-to-green consistency matters, that trajectory matters.

He's also got seven starts here with a top-10 finish, so he knows the setup.

The book's pricing him like he's a marginal make-cut candidate. He's not. At +107, you're getting a player the model sees as a 2-to-1 favorite to advance.

**Stake:** 1–2u. Make-cut bets are your floor play — high probability, low variance. This one's got real edge.

---

**One to avoid:** **Robert MacIntyre — Make Cut -155 (PointsBet)**

Yeah, he's got a 3.4pp edge and the model likes him at 64.2%. But the book's already priced him at 60.8% — they know what they're doing. The margin isn't worth the juice at -155. If you're playing make-cut, Thomas at +107 gives you way better value for essentially the same probability.
